transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-09-23   Time: 09:00 PT
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Devon Patel (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (BrightScale MLOps), Samir Rao (BrightScale CTO), Priya Menon (BrightScale FinOps)

Auto-generated summary (short):
BrightScale and Redwood reviewed current sprint health, emerging cost pressures from increased embedding usage, and reliability/latency regressions during peak. Customer reiterated need for VPC/private options and SOC2 evidence; Redwood AE/SE outlined pilot pricing scenarios, autoscale patterns, and a plan for a performance benchmark. Next steps and owners captured.

Topics covered:
- Usage trends (embeddings growth, peak qps)
- Cost vs latency trade-offs (dedicated vs hosted)
- Private deployment and compliance (SOC2, SSO, KMS)
- Performance benchmarks and runbook for POC
- Rollout and canary strategies (A/B, model variants)

Action items (captured in meeting notes): see action_items field

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hi everyone, thanks for hopping on. Quick roll call — Maya from Redwood, Devon our solutions engineer, and from BrightScale Lena, Samir and Priya. How are you all?
[00:12] Lena: Good, thanks. Busy sprint week but wanted to get this health check in.
[00:18] Samir: Yeah, we had a couple of late-night incidents last week so wanted to understand root cause and costs.
[00:25] Maya: Totally — that's the agenda, usage, cost, reliability and then follow-up pilot steps. Devon, want to kick off with what we saw on the infra side?
[00:32] Devon (Redwood SE): Sure. Quick context — we've been watching your embedding volume spike across the three product endpoints. Prefix/KV cache usage is high but prefix hit rate has been lower than expected because of variable prompt patterns — that drove extra decode tokens at peak and pushed p99 latency up to ~480 ms for some requests.
[00:55] Priya: Sorry can I jump in — when you say "embedding volume spike" can you quantify? We saw a billing jump but not sure which calls are dominant.
[01:02] Devon: Yeah, based on the samples you shared, embeddings accounted for ~63% of token spend last month and monthly embedding RPCs grew ~2.8x in the last 6 weeks.
[01:15] Priya: Ok that matches our bill. Oof.
[01:18] Lena: And the incidents — were they timeouts or throttles? Our app had some degraded responses.
[01:24] Devon: Mostly transient p99 spikes, plus one autoscale window hit where we saw capacity throttling. The platform fell back to a lower-cost variant in one zone — that's the graceful degradation kicking in, but it caused slightly different output behavior.
[01:40] Samir: That fallback changed the embeddings slightly and caused downstream mismatches in our vector-store similarity thresholds.
[01:47] Maya: Important callout. This is why we surfaced the model-variant mapping and the rollout policy in the deck we shared. You can pin a model or keep automatic fallback but if similarity consistency is critical you should pin or use Canary rollouts.
[02:05] Priya: On the cost side — we are evaluating Redwood Dedicated versus continuing hosted. Our finance team is worried about the sudden burn. What are the tradeoffs?
[02:15] Maya: Short version — Dedicated gives predictable committed capacity that dramatically reduces unit cost for high sustained throughput, and gives you isolation. Hosted is more flexible and better for bursty or experimental workloads. For your embedding profile, Dedicated with reserved capacity plus burst pool typically saves 30-45% at scale.
[02:36] Priya: 30-45% is compelling. Are there minimums or commit terms?
[02:40] Maya: Typical reserved terms are monthly or annual with step-down pricing for longer commitments. I'll send a few scenarios after this call — small/medium/large commit levels with modeled savings.
[02:51] Samir: We also need private deployment or VPC — we have compliance constraints. Can Redwood run in our VPC or on-prem?
[02:58] Devon: Yes — Redwood Private supports a VPC deployment and we have an on-prem option. For the VPC flow we provide a control plane with customer-managed networking and optional private endpoint. There are some onboarding steps — networking, KMS integration for customer keys, and the SOC2 evidence package.
[03:18] Lena: Speaking of SOC2 — do you have an SOC2 report and a pen-test summary we can share with our security team?
[03:23] Maya: We do. I'll share SOC2 Type II and our latest security pack. Also we can provide SSO/SAML metadata and RBAC docs.
[03:31] Samir: For encryption at rest and in transit — we need to route keys to our KMS.
[03:35] Devon: We support customer KMS/HSM integrations. We'll need your security contact to scope the key exchange and access control.
[03:42] Priya: Back to costs — what levers can we pull to reduce token spend without sacrificing latency?
[03:48] Devon: A few suggestions: better prefix caching (normalize prompts to increase cache hits), model quantization/64->16-bit tradeoffs for embeddings, batching where possible, and using a compact embedding model for lower-cost embeddings if similarity quality tolerates it. Also we have caching of embedding vectors for repeated content.
[04:05] Lena: About prompt normalization — we have many micro-templates. Would Redwood help with a prompt refactor or is that on us?
[04:12] Maya: We can do a short audit as part of the pilot — Devon can run a prompt and tokenization review and point out the highest ROI changes.
[04:20] Devon: Yep I can do that — I'll need a sample of typical prompts and anonymized payloads.
[04:24] Priya: For the pilot pricing, we want to see a scenario with committed capacity and one with hosted burst. Please include expected latencies.
[04:32] Maya: Will do. We'll include modeled p50/p90/p99 based on your sequence length distribution.
[04:37] [04:37] Samir: Quick technical question — when you say "KV cache" how is that managed across shards? We saw cache misses after a node restart.
[04:45] Devon: Our runtime maintains KV cache in process and we persist the cache across rolling restarts to reduce cold-starts, but if your request routing lands on a different shard without shared prefix cache you'll see misses. For strict low-latency guarantees we recommend pinned routing or warm-up policies.
[05:03] Lena: So pinned routing would ensure consistency, but what's the throughput impact?
[05:08] Devon: Pinning reduces flexibility in scheduling and can reduce overall cluster throughput slightly, but it improves latency stability. It's a classic latency vs throughput trade.
[05:18] Priya: Ok that helps.
[05:21] [05:21] Maya: I want to surface another thing — if you plan to move embeddings offline for batch indexing, we can recommend batching windows that save cost while keeping search freshness.
[05:31] Samir: We are considering nightly reindexes plus nearline updates. Can Redwood handle hybrid patterns?
[05:36] Devon: Yes — you can use a mix of hosted for nearline and dedicated/reserved for heavy nightly batch jobs. Our routing can target different model variants by route.
[05:46] Priya: There was mention of a "graceful degradation" that changed output — can we configure a fallback that keeps the same embedding model but a lower compute config?
[05:55] Devon: You can configure fallback policies to map to equivalent model variants (same architecture, different quantization) which helps reduce drift. The default fallback sometimes picks a compatible but slightly different model — we can make that stricter for you.
[06:10] Lena: That would be ideal — less drift during incidents.
[06:13] [06:13] Priya: Finance question — if we sign a 12-month reserved commitment, how do overages work?
[06:20] Maya: Typically overages are billed at a lower committed rate or drawn from a burst pool depending on the contract. We'll include detailed T&Cs in the scenarios.
[06:29] Samir: Ok, timeline for POC? We want to get meaningful numbers before our next budget review mid-Oct.
[06:35] Maya: We recommended a 3-week technical POC: week 1 onboarding + security, week 2 benchmarks and prompt audit, week 3 tuning and cost model. If we start the week of 9/29 we can deliver by mid-October.
[06:47] Priya: That timeline works if we get pricing model and security docs this week.
[06:52] Maya: We'll prioritize that. Devon, confirm runbook and data requests?
[06:56] Devon: I'll send a short runbook: sample dataset format, endpoints to hit, target p99 and throughput scenarios. Also include a script for local synthetic load to reproduce your observed p99.
[07:10] Lena: We'll prepare data and list of stakeholders.
[07:14] Samir: One last question on competitors — we ran a quick check vs ModelHostX and the price delta was similar but ModelHostX didn't have the VPC maturity. Does Redwood have marketplace references?
[07:25] Maya: Yes we can share reference customers for VPC and dedicated migrations. I'll include 2-3 case studies.
[07:32] Priya: Great.
[07:34] [07:34] Maya: Ok let's summarize next steps (quick): I'll send pilot pricing scenarios & SOC2/security pack by end of Thursday (2025-09-25), Devon will send benchmark runbook and data requests by Friday (2025-09-26), BrightScale will share sample prompts & volume numbers (Priya/Lena) by 2025-09-25. Schedule follow-up kickoff for week of 2025-09-29.
[07:55] Priya: Confirmed.
[07:57] Samir: Thanks all.
[07:59] Lena: Thanks.
[08:00] Maya: Thanks everyone, talk soon.

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-heard words — e.g., "dedikate" for "Dedicated" in auto transcript; proper nouns like "BrightScale" were sometimes split.
